chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Ahmad ibn Ishaq, from Bakr ibn Muhammad, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

A man asked him, and I was present, saying: 'A slave belongs to me who drinks wine and enters into these disliked matters (or: the matter of Wilayah, unwillingly). I intend to emancipate him. Is his emancipation more beloved to you, or should I sell him and give his price in charity?' He said: 'Emancipation is better in some times, and in some times charity is better. So when the people's state is good, emancipation is better. So when their state is severe (or: committing sins), charity is better. And selling this one is more beloved to me when he is in this state.'
ai.seo_question: When is it better to emancipate a slave versus selling them for charity according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) illustrates the principle of *fiqh al-awla* (jurisprudence of the more appropriate) by contextualizing slave emancipation against the broader spiritual state of the community. He distinguishes between times of general righteousness, where freeing a slave serves as a public exemplar of virtue, and times of moral decline, where selling and giving the price in charity is more effective for spiritual remediation. This nuanced ruling highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on dynamic legal reasoning (*ijtihad*) that adapts to changing social and ethical circumstances.

en.hubeali:
Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Ahmad Bin Is’haq, from Bakr Bin Muhammad, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said,

‘A man asked him<sup>asws</sup> and I was present, so he said, ‘There happens to be a slave for me, so he drank the wine, and he entered into this matter (Al-Wilayah) unwillingly. So I intend to emancipate him. So is his emancipation more beloved to you<sup>asws</sup>, or I sell him, and I give in charity with his price?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The emancipation is better in certain times, and in certain times the charity is better. So when the state of the people was good, so the emancipation is better. So when they state was difficult (committing sins), so the charity is preferable; and selling this one is more beloved to me<sup>asws</sup>, when he was in this state’.
